lines.text: Attention stores a key and a value for every head, for every layer, for every token.
That is a lot of duplication. Many heads end up storing almost the same key.
Group-query attention says: keep all the queries separate, but let a group of heads share one key and one value.
Eight query heads, one key and one value. Eight times less to store.
And the query still gets to be its own self, so each head can still look somewhere different.
Which sounds free. It is not, and the reason is a detail.
The shared key has to serve eight different queries, so it has to be the average of what those eight heads wanted.
Average keys are duller keys. The direction each head actually cared about gets smeared.
So quality does drop. The question is how much, and how fast it stops dropping.
DeepSeek went further and compressed the cache into a low-rank latent space instead.
Which gets the size down further, at the cost of rebuilding the keys on every step.
So the ladder is: share the heads, then compress them, then quantise what is left.
Every rung of that ladder is a trade, and the whole field is climbing it.
